notes: A finish_reason outside OpenAI's five values raises a pydantic ValidationError (ChatCompletion.model_validate), so the response is lost. Also reproduced on 1.33.3. The same error reaches provider='openai' pointed at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (ollama-openai). Fixed by a third-party PR (#1504); both cells PASS on 1.38.0.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. Ollama sends an id on each tool call, but the ollama Python client (0.6.3, latest) has no field for it, so any-llm's native provider generates UUIDs instead (providers/ollama/utils.py).

any-llm documents the fallback: a done_reason outside stop, length, tool_calls, content_filter and function_call is reported as stop (https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-llm/blob/18ed82b8ae89db560bf0b1ec8bccb752fc0e2b5d/src/any_llm/providers/ollama/utils.py#L33-L46). The caller cannot tell an unfamiliar reason from a normal stop.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores max_completion_tokens (v0.40.3), and any-llm's openai provider sends only that name (providers/openai/base.py), so the limit never applies. The root cause is in Ollama; the PR listed adds the field. The check reads the request any-llm sends, so the cell stays WRONG after Ollama's fix and re-recording does not change it: retire or rewrite the scenario when that release ships.

any-llm documents the fallback: a Gemini finish reason without an OpenAI counterpart (OTHER, LANGUAGE, MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL and any unfamiliar value) maps to None and a complete response then reports stop (https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-llm/blob/18ed82b8ae89db560bf0b1ec8bccb752fc0e2b5d/src/any_llm/providers/gemini/utils.py#L572-L581). The caller cannot tell such a stop from a normal one.

any-llm's Gemini provider builds call_{hash(function_call.name)}_{n} ids (providers/gemini/utils.py, non-stream and stream converters) and never reads FunctionCall.id, which google-genai exposes and Gemini sends. The ids also differ between processes because str hash() is salted. Reproduced on 1.33.0 and on main at 18ed82b. PR #1514 fixed the ids in 1.38.0 without linking this issue; the issue was closed on 2026-10-20.

any-llm documents the fallback: Anthropic stop reasons without an OpenAI counterpart (stop_sequence, pause_turn) fall through to stop, and the lookup defaults to stop for any unfamiliar value (https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-llm/blob/1.33.0/src/any_llm/providers/anthropic/utils.py#L40-L50, unchanged on main at 18ed82b). The caller cannot tell such a stop from a normal one.

A stream that ends before the provider's terminal signal returns the partial chunks normally, with no error and no incomplete flag (reproduced on 1.40.2 and 1.50.0). The OpenAI Responses path reports the output item as incomplete and passes.

LiteLLM deliberately normalizes unfamiliar finish reasons to stop with a warning. The upstream issue requested that fallback and is closed as completed; 1.105.1 implements it in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.105.1/litellm/litellm_core_utils/core_helpers.py#L253-L258. Gemini and the OpenAI Chat path retain the original in choices[0].provider_specific_fields.native_finish_reason; Anthropic and native Ollama normalize before assigning the choice and lose the original. A raw original does not change the contradictory primary stop.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. LiteLLM deliberately appends __thought__ and the thought signature to the provider's tool-call id for OpenAI client compatibility (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.105.1/litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/factory.py#L1163-L1179). Both suite cells preserve names, arguments and the second id, but the first id differs from the wire. The issue tracks interoperability failures caused by this encoding; the shim reports the exposed id unchanged.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. Native Ollama sends function.index 0 and 1 in separate chunks; LiteLLM does not lift that field to the delta tool-call index. Delta resets its default index to zero for each chunk, so ordinary index-based assembly merges two argument objects into one unparseable call (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.105.1/litellm/types/utils.py#L1555-L1573). The Ollama parser also replaces the wire ids with UUIDs, reported separately as https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/46543. Closed upstream on 2026-11-09: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/49183 gives each streamed tool call its own index on main, and the backport https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50718 shipped in v1.108.5 on lts/1.108.x. v1.109.0, the version tested, contains neither. The cell stays WRONG until the replaced ids (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/46543) are fixed too.

A stream that ends cleanly without any finish reason is reported with finish_reason stop. CustomStreamWrapper.finish_reason_handler falls back to stop when no finish reason was received (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.105.1/litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py#L1715-L1727). The Responses path keeps the missing finish and passes. Fixed by #47665, which doesn't link the issue: from 1.109.0 such a stream raises MidStreamFallbackError ("Stream ended before a finish_reason was received"). Gemini is still affected (next entry).

Still reported as stop in 1.109.0. The Gemini stream parser gives every chunk without finishReason finish_reason stop (_check_finish_reason falls back to stop: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.109.0/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py#L2477-L2490), so the wrapper sees a finish reason on every chunk and the end-of-stream check from #47665 never runs.

The native Ollama streaming parser replaces each tool-call id that Ollama sends with a random UUID once the arguments look complete (https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.105.1/litellm/llms/ollama/chat/transformation.py#L480-L489). Separate from the index-0 merge in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/33678; fixing that one alone leaves the ids wrong.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. PR #7096 added opt-in openai_chat_streaming_requires_finish_reason, deliberately retaining the default stop fallback for OpenAI-compatible APIs. In 2.56.0 the suite's default OpenAIProvider and OllamaProvider paths leave that flag false; clean EOF without a finish reason returns stop and a complete ModelResponse. The shim reads the library's response.state, without enabling the optional profile flag. See https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/v2.56.0/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/profiles/openai.py#L244-L249 and models/openai.py:4502-4513. This is not a default-path fix; the issue was opened on July 20 and the opt-in PR merged on September 2, 2026.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth. Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores max_completion_tokens (v0.40.3), and OllamaModel sends only that name (OllamaProvider keeps the OpenAI profile default, openai_chat_supports_max_completion_tokens=True), so the limit never applies. The root cause is in Ollama, as for any-llm; the check reads the request, so retire or rewrite the scenario when Ollama ships the fix.

Existing upstream issue, not opened by wiretruth; wiretruth's report, #10381, was closed as its duplicate. Up to 2.60.0, OpenAIChatModel re-validated the response with the strict ChatCompletion model (_validate_completion, models/openai.py), so a finish_reason outside OpenAI's five values raised UnexpectedModelBehavior and the text and usage were lost. OllamaModel inherits it. Since #11119 (2.61.0) the response is kept with finish_reason None and the raw value in provider_details['finish_reason'], so both cells move WRONG → LOSSY, the same as AnthropicModel, GoogleModel and OpenAIResponsesModel.

A stream that ends cleanly before the provider's terminal event finishes with ModelResponse.state 'complete' and finish_reason None, although the docs define 'incomplete' as a streamed response stopped before completion. Responses marks the response incomplete, but _ContinuationStreamedResponse.get() replaces it with complete once iteration ends; the Anthropic and Google adapters never set incomplete. The Chat Completions case is #6610 (documented-behavior). pydantic-ai's triage bot reproduced all three adapters and labelled the issue p:2-high and needs-maintainer-discussion (2026-10-25): the open question is whether a stream that ends before the provider's terminal event should report state 'incomplete'.

Existing upstream issue, opened by a maintainer, not by wiretruth. Cut-off structured output is retried, then fails with UnexpectedModelBehavior('Exceeded maximum output retries'); the length finish is only in the captured messages. https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/12406, merged after 2.66.0 and not in a release yet, raises right away with a message naming the token limit; https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/12407 (open) adds the typed OutputTokenLimitExceeded.

Reported in a comment on the token-limit issue: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues/12399#issuecomment-6780480981. Tool-call arguments cut off at the limit fail validation and end in the per-tool retry limit (UnexpectedModelBehavior: Tool 'create_event' exceeded max retries count of 0), not in IncompleteToolCall; reproduced on 2.61.0 and 2.66.0 with an ExternalToolset.
Same report as the entry above, for the streamed Anthropic cell (the non-streamed Anthropic cell passes).

A stream that ends cleanly before the provider's terminal event yields a normal finish part with finishReason 'other' and no error: the @ai-sdk/openai (Chat and Responses), @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/google adapters start from 'other' and emit it from flush(). vercel/ai#19165 fixed the same case in @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (an InvalidResponseDataError, then finish 'error'), so ollama-openai passes. Fixed by #23778, which adds an 'interrupted' finish reason in ai 7.0.149, and #23814, which makes the four adapters emit it when the stream ends without the provider's completion signal. The shim maps 'interrupted' to finish none and stream.completed false; all four cells pass on ai 7.0.153.

@ai-sdk/google's stream chunk schema has no error field, so an {"error": ...} SSE event after some content parses as an empty chunk: no error part, and the stream finishes with 'other'. Google's python-genai raises on such a chunk. Fixed by #23459 in @ai-sdk/google 4.0.99; the derived Gemini fixture passes on ai 7.0.146 (no live in-stream Gemini error has been observed).

The cause is in @google/genai, which @tanstack/ai-gemini streams through: processStreamResponse checks for an error object with JSON.parse on the raw network read, before the SSE data: prefix is removed, so an error event never matches; generateContentResponseFromMldev then drops the error field. chat() yields the partial text and ends with no RUN_ERROR or RUN_FINISHED. A bare JSON error body does throw ApiError. Google reproduced it on 2026-10-22 and opened #2094. The Gemini error-event fixture is derived (an error object injected into a recorded stream); no live mid-stream Gemini error has been observed.

Before 1.1.1, @tanstack/ai-ollama set the streamed RUN_FINISHED finishReason from whether tool calls were emitted (packages/ai-ollama/src/adapters/text.ts) and never read done_reason, so done_reason "length" finishes as stop. structuredOutput() already checks done_reason (TanStack/ai#1548). Fixed by #2077 (@tanstack/ai-ollama 1.1.1): done_reason "length" now finishes as length; the cell is PASS on the 1.4.0 results.

@tanstack/openai-base Chat Completions picks tool_calls over a pending finish_reason "length" once TOOL_CALL_END was emitted for the unfinished arguments. The core then treats the arguments as a parse failure and the agent loop sends the conversation back to the model: 5 requests in the fixture replay. Fixed by #1874: a pending 'length' now wins over the tool-call flag, so 1.0.0 reports length and sends one request.

The Gemini adapter emits RUN_FINISHED only for a chunk with finishReason; a stream that ends without one stops with no terminal event and no error (@tanstack/ai-gemini 1.2.1). The Anthropic adapter got a terminal outcome for the same case in @tanstack/ai-anthropic 1.1.1 (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/pull/2042).
